title: introduce-cmk-consent-middleware-and-audit-shredder
author: Nadia Chen
description:
Motivation: Some customers require explicit consent before the platform may use their CMKs (customer-managed keys) for operations that cross region boundaries or are forwarded to downstream providers. Additionally, long-form audit records occasionally contain high-sensitivity headers and request payload fragments that are unnecessary for investigations and increase data residency surface area. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces of work: 1) a CMK Consent Middleware that enforces opt-in consent signals and provenance for CMK usage and 2) an Audit Shredder component that strips or tokens sensitive header/payload snippets for tenants with strict residency/compliance profiles.

What this changes (high level):
- Runtime: new middleware hook in runtime/controlplane that validates a tenant's consent profile before permitting CMK selection and wrap/unwrap operations. If consent is not present, the request is rejected with a clear error and remediation link.
- Audit: an Audit Shredder service runs as part of the audit pipeline and applies tenant-configurable shredding rules (header allowlist, fixed-length tokenization of id fragments, and deterministic hashing of sensitive substrings). Shredding policies are enforced for tenants with residency=EU or policy flag require_shred=true.
- Config/DB: schema additions to tenant profiles: `consent_provenance` (enum: explicit, delegated, legacy) and `shred_policy_id`. Includes migration that defaults legacy tenants to delegated for backwards compatibility but marks them as needing re-consent.
- Observability/SLA: adds metrics and spans for consent-check latency, consent-denied counters, shred-rate, and audit size delta.
- Rollout: feature-flag gated and introduced behind a canary rollout. Default behaviour unchanged for most tenants. Admin UI changes to surface consent state are included in a follow-up PR (linked).

Checklist: 
- [x] Runtime CMK hook and middleware (integration + unit tests)
- [x] Audit Shredder component and pipeline integration
- [x] Tenant schema migration and migration tool tests
- [x] Metrics and tracing instrumentation
- [x] Documentation: short security appendix and dev notes included in repo (docs/security/cmk-consent.md)
- [x] Backwards-compatible defaults and feature flag

Behavior notes and failure modes: 
- If the consent check times out, the request fails with 429 and is routed to a lightweight fallback that uses platform-managed keys (if tenant policy allows).
- Shredder is conservative: it never modifies cryptographic envelopes (wrapped CMKs) but can redact headers and request text.
- Tenant migration sets `consent_provenance=delegated` for older accounts; admins must complete re-consent flows for `explicit` enforcement.

Why this is different from prior KMS/regional PRs: many previous changes focused on region pinning and assertion propagation. This PR focuses on explicit customer consent as a first-class policy signal that gates cryptographic operations and reduces audit data residency risk by shredding unnecessary sensitive fields earlier in the pipeline.

Related: Linear ENG-4821, SEC-199, SUP-7321. Follow-up: UI work (PR TBD) to allow tenant admins to view/record consent provenance.

review_comments: Marco Rivera (reviewer): Can we add a metric for requests denied due to lack of explicit consent? Need that for SLO impact analysis.
Nadia Chen (author): Added consent_denied_total and a histogram for consent_check_latency in pkg/metrics; also added tests for metric emission.
Priya Singh (security): The shredder rules look good, but ensure deterministic hashing uses tenant-specific salt stored in KMS and is non-reversible. Also please document the salt rotation behaviour.

Nadia Chen (author): Updated rules_engine.go to pull tenant salt from KMS via the KMS accessor interface; added note in docs about rotation causing stable token mismatch for older logs and recommended retention policy.
Eliot Park (sre): I saw a flaky integration test in CI (audit pipeline e2e) — looks timing-related. Can we increase timeouts or make the test poll for readiness?
Nadia Chen (author): Increased test polling with exponential backoff; CI passed on rerun (see CI entries).

release_notes: Add CMK consent middleware to gate customer-managed-key usage and introduce an Audit Shredder to redact tenant-sensitive headers and payload fragments. This is behind a feature flag and rolled out as a canary. Admins of legacy tenants should follow the re-consent migration procedure.
